Q: Parsing Binance API kline timestamps — off by 7 hours in my local time? A:

The date/time data you retrieve from BTC candlestick charts appears to be 7 hours behind your local time and your time zone is UTC+7, that means the data is UTC+0.

To convert it to your local time without hard-coding the offset before it's saved to CSV file or displayed on console, you can use the astimezone() instance method provided by datetime class from datetime module:

local_time = utc0_date_time_value.astimezone()

The result local_time will also have the type datetime but the value is augmented with local time-zone offset.

If your data is retrieve from the source as string value, you can covert it to datetime value like so (suppose the data is in YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss format):

from datetime import datetime

date_time_string = "2026-08-13 10:20:30"
date_time_value = datetime.strptime(date_time_string, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
local_time = date_time_value.astimezone()

Q: MySQL error using query containing "SELECT DISTINCT TOP 2" previously running in a MS SQL database A:

I think that this can be simplified as follows...

SELECT DISTINCT YEAR(res_created) responseYear
  FROM Responses r
  JOIN Questions q
    ON q.question_id = r.question_id 
  JOIN Lookup_Survey_Questions lsq
    ON lsq.question_id = q.question_id 
  JOIN Survey u
    ON u.survey_id = lsq.survey_id
  JOIN School c
    ON c.sch_id = u.sch_id
  JOIN Authority a
    ON a.auth_id = c.auth_id
 WHERE a.auth_id = #arguments.authorityID#
   AND q.question_id = #arguments.questionID#
   AND c.auth_id=#arguments.authorityID#
 ORDER 
    BY responseYear ASC
 LIMIT 2;

Q: How can I read my app's database file from device? A:

You can view (visualize) the data in the .db file by using the software called "DB Browser for SQLITE"

  1. get your .db file from the device(smartphone) memory (by accessing the DDMS --> File explore)
  2. download and install sqlitebrowser (http://sqlitebrowser.org/)
  3. after installing, open "DB Browser for SQLITE" and go to "open database" to load your .db file
  4. Choose the "Browse data" tab
  5. Finally, select the table you want to visualize to display the data in the database.

Q: compare data with month from previous year in Qlikview A:

You can solve this problem at the script side while loading data. So that you can compare year to date data with previous year with until corresponding month.

Transaction_Table:
 LOAD date,productID,amount
 FROM data.qvd;

concatenate

 Load AddYears(date,1) as date,productID,amount_1
 Resident data where date<=AddYears($(=max(date)),-1);

There will be two coloumns "amount" is current date's data and "amount_1" is previous year's same day data.
